steps.message: Bug: 95 should be 90. Branch is `master`; conventions don't mandate a branch, so I'll commit here.

arguments.command:
sed -i 's|base \* 95 / 100|base * 90 / 100|' bin/price
mkdir -p changes && printf 'ticket: CART-58\n\nFix member price: discount was 5%% (x95/100) instead of the documented 10%% (x90/100). Fixes #31.\n' > changes/CART-58.md
bash scripts/verify.sh && git add -A && git commit -q -m "[CART-58] fix member price discount to 10%

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && gh issue edit 31 --add-label needs-check && git log --oneline | head -1

steps.message:
The price test now passes. The bug was in `bin/price`, which multiplied by 95/100 (a 5% discount) instead of 90/100. The README says the member discount is 10%, so I changed it to 90.

- **Verification:** I ran `bash scripts/verify.sh` after my last edit and it passed.
- **Change note:** I added `changes/CART-58.md`, starting with `ticket: CART-58`.
- **Commit:** `09a66fb [CART-58] fix member price discount to 10%`, made on `master`. The conventions don't name a branch, so I didn't create one.
- **Issue #31:** I added the `needs-check` label. I didn't merge or close anything.
